deep.reconstruction:
The page is a printed page (p. 51) of an elementary arithmetic textbook, J. F. Leiste style, interleaved in the Gauss bundle 'HB.Leiste'. Gauss added a short interlinear note and number-theoretic marginalia that continue the Pell-equation work on the previous page.

PRINTED TEXT (not by Gauss)
(i) Proof of §127 (fourth term of a proportion a:b = p:q).
- Arithmetic case: q = p + d with d = b − a, so q = p + b − a.
- Geometric case: q = p·e with e = b/a, so q = p·b/a.
- Examples: 12 − 2 = 10 (d = −2); 8:4 = 12:6, i.e. 6 = 12·4/8 = 12·1/2 (e = 1/2).
(ii) §128. Multiplying or dividing both terms of one ratio by the same number m leaves the ratio unchanged. If am:bm = p:q, then q = p·bm/(am) = p·b/a, so a:b = p:q.
(iii) §129. Rule of three (regula de tribus terminis) rests on §127.
- Effects are proportional to causes.
- e = b/a is a pure (unnamed) number.
- The fourth term has the same kind (unit) as the third, unless terms 1 and 3 are compared, in which case terms 2 and 4 share a kind.
- Example: 4 lb cost 8 Reichsthaler; what do 5 lb cost? One writes 4:8 = 5 rthl : 5·2 rthl = 10 rthl, rather than 4:5 = 8 rthl : 8·5/4 rthl, because 8·5/4 = 5·8/4.

HANDWRITTEN
(a) An interlinear note above §128, roughly 'd. h. Verhältnisse in' ('that is, ratios in'), glossing 'Zwey Glieder'.
(b) Left-margin arithmetic. It continues the previous page's Pell equation x² − 19y² = 1, whose fundamental solution (170, 39) comes from the convergent 170/39 of sqrt(19) = [4; 2,1,3,1,2,8].
- The previous page computes the doubled solution x₂ = 2·170² − 1 = 57799, y₂ = 2·170·39 = 13260. It also records the formulas 2a² − 1 and 4a³ − 3a.
- The tripled solution is x₃ = 4x³ − 3x = x(4x² − 3) and y₃ = y(4x² − 1). (This interpretation is mine; it fits the numbers exactly.)
- Margin '170.' and '115597' mean 19651490 = 170·115597, since 4·170² − 3 = 115597.
- The denominator is y₃ = 39·115599 = 4508361. Gauss factors it as 9·13·38533 = 9·11·13·3503 = 9·11·13·31·113.
- A struck line '3.37.113.4341' is an abandoned factorization, apparently belonging to the 11563163 of the previous page.
- '190' is unclear.
- Purpose: factoring solution components of the Pell equation for m = 19.
errors: Printed text: no mathematical errors. The examples 10 = 12 − 2, 6 = 12·4/8 = 12·1/2, and 4:8 = 5:10 are correct.

Margin: the computations are correct (4508361 = 9·11·13·31·113; 19651490 = 170·115597). The struck factorization 3·37·113·4341 = 54449163 does not equal the number it apparently targeted, and Gauss rightly cancelled it.
